reports.title: Parker Delivers Record Fiscal 2027 First Quarter Results, Raises Full Year Outlook

guidance.heading: Fiscal 2027 Outlook
section: The company has updated guidance for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, which now includes Filtration Group Corporation.
•Organic sales growth of 7.5% to 10.5%; acquisitions of 9%, and currency of (0.5%)
•Segment operating margin of 23.6% to 24.0%, or 27.7% to 28.1% on an adjusted basis
•EPS of $29.65 to $30.45, or $36.45 to $37.25 on an adjusted basis

desk.headline: Sales up 18% to a record $6.0bn and adjusted EPS up 23% to $8.90, beat; full-year adjusted EPS outlook raised to $36.45–37.25
results: Sales rose 18% to a record $6.0bn: 11.5% organic growth plus 7% from acquisitions.
Adjusted EPS climbed 23% to a record $8.90; GAAP EPS rose 10% to $6.92 after Filtration Group deal costs and higher amortisation.
Adjusted segment margin hit a record 28.6% (up 120 bps); Aerospace reached 30.7% on 14% organic growth, and Asia-Pacific industrial sales grew 23% organically.
Rolling 12-month orders were up 13% and backlog reached a record $13.7bn.
The Filtration Group acquisition closed (about $9.1bn spent on acquisitions in the quarter), lifting total debt to about $17.5bn; quarterly dividend is $2.00, up from $1.80.

guidance.summary: Parker lifted its fiscal 2027 (year to June 2027) outlook, now including Filtration Group: adjusted EPS $36.45–37.25 (was $34.25–35.25) and organic growth 7.5–10.5% (was 5.5–8.5%). GAAP EPS guidance slips to $29.65–30.45 on deal-related costs.

points: Demand rose in every market vertical, with double-digit order growth across all businesses; distributor orders also grew by double digits.
Aerospace aftermarket is supported by ageing fleets and few aircraft retirements; commercial OEM is guided to mid-teens growth.
Filtration Group should add about $1.85bn of sales and $0.50 of adjusted EPS this year, with $40m of cost savings now and a $220m longer-term target; no revenue synergies assumed.
Q2 guide: sales of nearly $6.2bn and adjusted EPS of about $8.82; data centres are a small (~1.5% of sales) but fast-growing business.
Net debt rose to 2.7 times EBITDA after the deal, and interest cost is now guided at $690m for the year; pricing was described as margin neutral.
call.source: Call coverage: TradingKey call summary, 5 Nov 2026; StockStory, 6 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Integration of Filtration Group and delivery of the first $40m of cost savings.
Whether order growth and the record backlog keep organic growth near 10%.
Debt reduction after the deal and the higher interest bill.
